applicable_when: The kernel performs a tiny GEMM (M=8388608, N=6, K=3) with BLOCK_K=16 and BLOCK_N=16 — both massively oversized relative to the actual K=3 and N=6 dimensions. This causes: (1) 9.5-way shared memory bank conflicts because the tl.dot tile layout conflicts with the shared memory banking pattern for these non-power-of-2 effective dimensions; (2) only 11.2/32 bytes utilized per global load sector due to the strided A matrix (stride_am=3, stride_ak=1 — channel-last layout); (3) 160 registers/thread crushing occupancy to 18.75% and leaving the scheduler starved 74% of cycles. On H200 (Hopper), switching to tl.make_block_ptr / TMA-style loads offloads address generation to the TMA hardware unit, reduces scalar pointer arithmetic overhead, enables asynchronous bulk copies, and — combined with right-sized tile parameters — dramatically reduces register pressure and bank conflicts.
